# ISSUE-57 implementation plan

Make isolated agent deadlines policy-driven and retain recoverable work without importing failed runs.

**Shape: Involved.** This crosses config validation, trusted policy propagation, four interactive harness loops, OCI lifecycle, safe filesystem export, and checkpoint exclusion. Keep it one WorkUnit because these pieces jointly establish the timeout safety contract; require the configured independent agent plan gate before implementation. No protected harness changes are needed.

## What we know

- `internal/agent/isolated.go:41` supplies a 15-minute timeout; `internal/sandbox/native.go:357` and `internal/sandbox/worker.go:346` independently cap execution at 15 minutes. Both workspace paths return on execution failure before importing results and defer snapshot/container cleanup.
- `internal/contract/execution.go:17` defines execution policy; `internal/harness/scaffold.go:563` (`decodeConfig`) already invokes `ResolveExecution`, so central duration validation can reach doctor and validate without changing repository policy files.
- Execution uses approved configuration (`internal/workflow/engine.go:247,434`, `internal/cli/claim_helpers.go:38`); `NewConfiguredRunner` currently retains boundary settings but no timeout policy (`internal/agent/configured.go`). Never reload config inside a worker.
- Coordinator-owned input waits exist in `RunNativeCodex`, `RunDelegatedHarness`, `runOpenCode`, and `runOMP` (`internal/sandbox/native.go:296`, `delegated.go:94`, `opencode.go:23`, `omp.go:20`). OMP waits until session settlement before asking for input; tool activity is not operator idle time.
- Native validation also uses `withNativeWorkspace`; OCI validation supplies its check duration with `DiscardChanges` (`internal/validation/validator.go:150`). Agent budget changes must not change validation-check timeout semantics.
- Recovery needs explicit publication exclusion: `Checkpoint` uses `git add -A` (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:375`), and snapshot packing excludes several coordinator directories but not all active-output files (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:638`).
- `safeRunFailure` deliberately masks error strings (`internal/agent/failure.go:19`); a recovery error must expose only coordinator-generated metadata through that wrapper.
- `internal/safefs/root.go` provides pinned roots, safe directory creation, regular-file checks, and atomic replacement. Existing snapshot pack/unpack rejects unsafe entries. OCI read-only outputs live in `/output`, with coordinator-installed links in `/workspace` (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:405`).

## What we're assuming

- A configured timeout is the cumulative working budget for interactive native runs; interactive OCI uses the configured duration when explicitly provided, bounded by four hours, and otherwise defaults to four hours. Unattended defaults to one hour. Confirm this interpretation against the acceptance criteria during plan review; document it identically in resolver tests, doctor output, and config reference.
- A modest recovery bound (proposed 8 MiB total, with per-file and entry limits) is useful. Confirm against existing worker budgets in step 1; omit whole oversized/binary entries with explicit coordinator-generated notices rather than truncating a hunk into an invalid diff.

## Open questions

- Can each supported OCI runtime pause/export after deadline cancellation without losing tmpfs? Step 1 uses existing fake-runtime fixtures to establish the recovery sequence; optional local runtime checks confirm it. No new image or turn protocol.
- Which checkpoint/submission paths can include an already tracked or staged recovery file? Step 1 traces them and step 6 adds an explicit rejection/exclusion regression; an ignore rule alone is insufficient.

## Design and alternatives

Use a single pure resolver in `internal/contract` and a shared coordinator-owned budget controller in `internal/sandbox`. Retain the resolved policy on the configured adapter. A single wall-clock context cannot exclude operator think-time; resetting a timeout each turn incorrectly grants unlimited aggregate working time. Instead track cumulative active time across turns and a separate fixed four-hour interactive wall deadline. Pause active accounting only immediately around coordinator-owned input reads, never based on output silence or model-supplied timestamps. Parent cancellation always wins.

Capture recovery from a validated immutable baseline and stopped/frozen sandbox, never from the live checkout or by applying changes. Use the same recovery writer for native, delegated, and OCI backends, including read-only role output mapping. Recovery is diagnostic local output, never a successful role artifact. Keep validation execution separate from agent budgets; do not add timeout flags unless a real existing override path requires plumbing. Any operator override must be positive and may only reduce policy.

## Files, symbols, and sequence

1. Inspect existing worker manifests/budgets, snapshot import rules, OCI stop/pause/export behavior, `RunNativeValidation`, and all checkpoint/submission paths. Add small deterministic lifecycle fixtures to settle the open questions before changing execution. If safe OCI export cannot be established with current runtime primitives, stop for plan revision rather than silently reducing acceptance.
2. Extend `ExecutionConfig` in `internal/contract/execution.go` with string `AgentTimeout` and per-role `RoleTimeouts` (YAML/JSON names from the contract). Add `ResolveAgentTimeout` and resolved budget type in new `internal/contract/timeout.go`. Parse Go durations; distinguish omitted from explicitly empty values, reject non-positive/overflow/malformed durations and unknown role keys; validate every override even for unselected roles. Call validation from `ResolveExecution`. Default unattended active budget to 60m; interactive wall cap is 4h; native interactive active budget defaults to 60m, OCI interactive has no idle exclusion. Role overrides take precedence over the global value. Resolve warning lead as min(2m, 10% of the applicable budget). No new config keys beyond those requested.
3. In `internal/agent/configured.go`, `adapters.go` (`CLIAdapter`), and `isolated.go` (`runIsolated`), retain approved execution policy and pass a resolved budget, role, interactive mode, and coordinator warning sink via `WorkerOptions`. Audit runner construction in workflow/project planning and CLI paths to preserve approved-base loading; add regression fixtures in `internal/agent/isolation_policy_test.go` and `internal/workflow/engine_test.go` (or a focused new timeout-policy test file). Candidate config never supplies execution authority.
4. Add `internal/sandbox/timeout.go` with an injectable clock/timer, cumulative active accounting, immutable wall cap, cancellation cause, and synchronized once-only warning for the first impending effective deadline. Stop timers/goroutines on every exit; do not let resume race with cancellation. Integrate `withNativeWorkspace` and `RunWorker`; remove hardcoded agent caps. In `native.go`, `delegated.go`, `opencode.go`, and `omp.go`, pause only while `nativeInstruction` awaits input and resume before dispatch. Keep setup, tool execution, and session settlement charged. Warnings name validated role and remaining duration and reach stderr/interactive terminal even while input is blocked. Validation uses its existing caller/check contexts and explicit check timeout, with no recovery patch or agent-default substitution.
5. Add `internal/sandbox/timeout_patch.go`: compare initial snapshot bytes with final validated regular files, produce deterministic relative-path unified diffs for additions/modifications/deletions and role output files, bound input reads, diff computation, entries, output bytes, and recovery elapsed time. Include useful handling of no-final-newline, binary, and oversized files. Reject traversal, symlinks, hardlinks, FIFOs/devices/sockets and unsafe destination components; do not follow candidate paths. Write only `.swarm/active-output/<validated-role>-timeout.patch` via `safefs.Root.Sub`/`WriteFile`, mode 0600. On deadline, terminate/quiesce native processes and tools before capture; pause OCI before bounded export, read `/output` for read-only roles, then remove the container. Recovery uses a separate short coordinator context because the run context has expired, and never calls `importWorker` or role-output replacement. Preserve timeout classification if capture fails and report capture failure honestly; never claim a patch exists until atomic write succeeds.
6. Add a typed timeout error containing only trusted role, effective limit/deadline kind, and fixed relative patch path. Update `internal/agent/failure.go` to render this metadata while continuing to mask arbitrary harness diagnostics and preserve `errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded)`. Exclude timeout patches from sandbox inputs/outputs in `worker.go`; update `internal/workspace/worktree.go` (`Checkpoint` and local excludes) and the actual submission guards found in step 1 to keep recovery files out even if staged/tracked. Add a guard before publication where needed; never mutate checkpoint/state/artifacts on timeout.
7. In `internal/cli/doctor.go`, add deterministic per-role resolved timeout reporting, including interactive active/wall semantics. Doctor describes the local repository config; actual runs continue to use the approved base. Verify errors flow through `internal/harness/scaffold.go:decodeConfig` and `internal/validation/validator.go` before checks execute. Extend existing CLI/harness tests.
8. Update `docs/project.md` config reference, `docs/developer.md` interrupted-run recovery, `docs/harness/README.md`, `codex.md`, `claude.md`, `opencode.md`, `omp.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`. Explain global/per-role precedence, budgets, warning lead, OCI wall-only accounting, patch limits, and manual inspection/recovery. Keep existing per-tool deadlines distinct and unchanged. Do not change `.swarm/config.yaml`, protected schemas/prompts/workflows, validation checks, or CI.
9. Run TEST_PLAN checks and inspect the final diff for unplanned policy or publication changes. All security regression cases must fail against old behavior; retain existing adversarial coverage.

# ISSUE-57 verification plan

These are implementation-phase checks; planning does not claim they have passed. Use fake clocks and subprocess/fake-runtime fixtures, without model calls or a new OCI image. Add table-driven tests to existing package suites or focused `timeout_test.go`/`timeout_patch_test.go` files.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Config keys and invalid values | Contract tables cover omitted defaults, Go duration syntax, explicit empty, zero, negative, malformed and overflowing values, unknown roles, and invalid unselected overrides. Harness config decode and CLI fixtures require field-qualified failures from doctor and repo validate before execution. Repo validate uses a full trusted fixture base commit. | `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/cli ./internal/validation` |
| 2. Defaults, idle exclusion, wall cap, shared resolver | Resolver tables cover all four roles, global values, role precedence, unattended 60m, native/delegated interactive cumulative active budget and 4h wall cap, OCI interactive 4h default and configured shorter limits. Fake clock advances through multiple turns: idle adds no active time, work accumulates, resuming never resets budget, wall timeout still fires during idle. Cover Codex, Claude, OpenCode, and OMP coordinator input boundaries; OMP pending tools/session settlement still count. Assert backend parity and positive operator overrides cannot extend policy. Validation check deadlines remain independent, including explicit limits longer than the agent default. | `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/agent ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation` |
| 3. Warning | Fake-clock boundary tests check min(2m, 10%), role/remaining-time text, one warning across pause/resume and competing wall/active thresholds, no warning after completion, and concurrent deadline/cancellation cleanup. Capture interactive stderr while blocked on input and headless progress output. | `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent` |
| 4. Recovery and unchanged worktree | Native/delegated execution and fake OCI fixtures modify/add/delete files then expire. Verify correct fixed relative patch path and configured limit survive safe error masking; `errors.Is` retains DeadlineExceeded. Apply a complete text patch only in a disposable scratch fixture to verify its content. Compare checkout files, index, HEAD, existing PLAN/TEST_PLAN/REVIEW and lease artifact/checkpoint state before/after: only local recovery output may differ. Cover read-only output mapping, timeout during input, cumulative active timeout, and wall timeout. Cancellation/non-timeout failure must not masquerade as policy timeout. | `go test ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace` |
| 5. Doctor displays roles | CLI output fixture asserts planner/reviewer/developer/tester values, stable order, configured override, defaults, and interactive accounting/cap in text and existing JSON output. Invalid config produces nonzero exit with the offending field. | `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/harness` |
| 6. Required security/default regressions and make check | Commit trusted fixture config, change candidate timeout to a larger value, and verify the runner still expires at the trusted value; candidate invalid config also cannot replace approved authority. Exercise planner/reviewer/developer/tester construction. Reject symlink ancestors/destinations, linked source files, traversal, absolute paths, hardlinks, FIFO/device/socket entries without blocking or reading outside the sandbox. Bound file count, binary/oversized entries, diff size, and recovery time; no partial unsafe artifact, and failure preserves the timeout cause. Test poisoned existing output, write failure, repeated recovery replacement, once-only warnings under race detector, OCI freeze/export/removal ordering, export failure cleanup, and all descendants stopped before native capture. Ensure timeout patch never imports, becomes a role artifact, enters a later snapshot, checkpoint, or submission, including pre-staged/tracked patches. | `go test -race ./internal/contract ./internal/agent ./internal/sandbox ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace ./internal/pr ./internal/cli ./internal/validation`; `make check` |
| 7. Documentation | Review actual config tags against all examples; verify docs/project.md, recovery section in docs/developer.md, relevant harness limit guides and CHANGELOG.md are updated. Check relative links/anchors and parse changed bash blocks with `bash -n`; compare documented commands with Cobra registrations/help. Explain OCI wall-only accounting and manual patch recovery; preserve tool and validation deadlines. | `go run ./cmd/swarm repo doctor --help`; `go run ./cmd/swarm repo validate --help`; `git diff --check` plus link/snippet checks |

Implementation completion sequence:

```bash
make fmt
go build ./...
go test ./...
go vet ./...
make check
git diff --check
```

Run `make install` with a writable temporary `GOBIN` for the required hands-on CLI build, then inspect its `repo doctor --help` and `repo validate --help`. A real local OCI runtime smoke test is supplemental when available; required lifecycle coverage must run without a qualification image. Record skipped environmental checks and actual command outcomes in validation artifacts. Do not run coordinator claim/publication commands from the agent.
